questions.question: How do you test probabilistic LLM output without making tests flaky?
questions.model_answer: Separate deterministic assertions from semantic metrics, use a representative golden dataset, calibrate thresholds, and avoid exact-string checks for probabilistic output.

questions.question: What is the difference between retrieval quality and answer grounding?
questions.model_answer: Retrieval quality checks whether the correct documents were retrieved using Precision@K and Recall@K; grounding checks whether answer claims are supported by retrieved context.

questions.question: How do you test an autonomous browser agent beyond task completion?
questions.model_answer: Validate tool/element grounding, separate decision retries from execution failures, inspect trajectory/step efficiency, detect loops and use dataset-level quality gates.

questions.question: Why should decision retry and execution retry be separate?
questions.model_answer: Semantic invalidity needs re-planning with feedback; a transient tool failure may retry the same already-valid action.

questions.question: How would you test an MCP tool integration?
questions.model_answer: Test runtime discovery/schema, argument normalization/validation, execution behavior, and separately verify business task completion.

questions.question: What must be tested in a multi-agent system besides each agent individually?
questions.model_answer: Test routing, handoff contracts, context preservation, dependency order, downstream interpretation, failure propagation and loops.

questions.question: Where should prompt injection be blocked in an agent system?
questions.model_answer: Use layered defense: input guard before planning, handoff validation at agent boundaries, and least-privilege policy before tool execution.

questions.question: An agent passes functionally but becomes 5x slower. Is that a release pass?
questions.model_answer: Not necessarily. Functional correctness is one gate; operational quality uses latency budgets and regression baselines and can block release.

questions.question: How do you measure agent flakiness?
questions.model_answer: Repeat identical scenarios and measure pass rate, mixed outcomes, latency variability, retry overhead and failure streaks.

questions.question: Would you run live LLM/browser-agent tests on every pull request?
questions.model_answer: Keep fast deterministic tests on PRs and expensive live LLM/MCP/browser tests on scheduled, manual or release pipelines.

questions.question: How is AI API testing different from ordinary API testing?
questions.model_answer: Test ordinary schema/status/performance plus probabilistic quality, safety, model latency, malformed outputs and provider resilience.

questions.question: When should LLM-as-Judge not be the hard release gate?
questions.model_answer: When deterministic ground truth exists or the judge is not calibrated; test the evaluator itself and prefer deterministic evidence for hard gates.

questions.question: Describe a production AI testing architecture you have built.
questions.model_answer: Layer LLM/RAG evaluations, MCP/tool testing, agent trajectory tests, multi-agent handoffs, deterministic guardrails, observability/reliability and CI release gates.

questions.question: What if an LLM faithfulness judge fails but deterministic ground truth proves support?
questions.model_answer: Treat it as evaluator calibration, inspect the judge, keep ground truth as the hard gate and do not lower thresholds just to get green.

questions.question: How do you detect an agent stuck loop?
questions.model_answer: Normalize decision signatures, detect consecutive repetitions over a threshold, and keep a max-step guard.

questions.question: Why should token or cost metrics be nullable instead of zero when unavailable?
questions.model_answer: Zero means measured zero usage; unavailable means unknown. Using zero for missing telemetry is misleading and corrupts cost gates.

questions.question: What does latency coefficient of variation tell you?
questions.model_answer: CV is standard deviation divided by mean and normalizes latency variability, making stability comparable across scenarios with different average latency.

questions.question: What extra tests are needed for Agentic RAG compared with normal RAG?
questions.model_answer: Test whether retrieval was invoked when needed, routing/tool decisions, retrieval metrics, citations and grounding, plus loops and unnecessary retrieval.

questions.question: Which performance metric is more useful than average latency for an AI API?
questions.model_answer: P95 or P99 exposes tail latency and better represents slow user experiences than the average alone.

questions.question: How do you combine many AI quality signals into a release decision?
questions.model_answer: Use component-specific thresholds, critical hard gates for safety/functionality, dataset-level aggregation and explicit regression checks rather than one blended score.
